task.title: Escape untrusted corpus record paths in CLI output
task.objective: Keep untrusted filenames inside one deterministic quoted field without terminal controls, forged lines, or collapsed Unix path identities
acceptance_criteria: Inspector rows and diagnostics share one quoted path representation
Control-bearing paths do not emit literal newline, carriage return, tab, or escape bytes
Each row and diagnostic remains one physical line
Distinct non-UTF-8 Unix paths remain distinguishable

attempts.summary: Added an inspector regression with newline and escape bytes in a filename
attempts.diagnostic: The prior output produced three physical stdout lines instead of two

attempts.summary: Added shared quoted path rendering for inspector rows and corpus diagnostics
Changed rendering to debug-format Path directly and expanded control-byte coverage after review
attempts.diagnostic: Debug-formatting path.display() was lossy for invalid Unix bytes and could collapse distinct filenames to the same replacement character

outcome.summary: Corpus CLI output now quotes untrusted paths without physical-line injection, raw controls, or lossy Unix filename identity

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-dev --test cli corpus_
GitHub Rust quality gate for PR 1118

lessons: Debug-format Path itself rather than its lossy display adapter when diagnostic identity matters
Control-safe output tests should assert escaped text and the absence of raw control bytes
